# Kyoto Spring Itinerary for 2 Adults

A moderate-pace Kyoto plan for **2026-04-10 to 2026-04-13** with **temples, quiet neighborhoods, local food, one evening activity, public transit**, and **low-walk routing**. Estimated total stays within your **JPY 180,000** budget excluding flights.

## 4-Day Kyoto Plan by Neighborhood

### Day 1: Higashiyama Welcome Walk
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- **Morning:** Arrive, check in, and keep the first block light with a taxi or short bus ride to your hotel.
- **Afternoon:** Visit **Kiyomizu-dera** using the shortest practical route; focus on the main temple grounds and nearby viewpoints, then take a taxi back down if needed.
- **Food:** Early dinner in Gion/Higashiyama with **yudofu** or **soba**; choose a restaurant close to the stop to reduce walking.
- **Evening:** Optional gentle stroll in **Gion’s lantern-lit streets**; keep it short and seated where possible.

### Day 2: Arashiyama and Western Kyoto
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/tree.svg
- **Morning:** Take JR or Hankyu plus a short taxi to **Tenryu-ji** and the surrounding temple area.
- **Afternoon:** Enjoy **Arashiyama Bamboo Grove** only as a brief pass-through, then spend more time at a riverside café or the **Okochi Sanso** area if energy allows.
- **Food:** Lunch on **tofu set meals** or **yuba** near Arashiyama Station.
- **Evening:** Return early to the hotel and rest; keep this as a recovery day.

### Day 3: Quiet Temples and Local Neighborhoods
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/geo-alt.svg
- **Morning:** Visit **Daitoku-ji** or **Shisen-do** for a calmer temple experience with fewer crowds.
- **Afternoon:** Move to **Demachiyanagi** or **Nishijin** for a slower neighborhood feel, with a tea stop and a short local shopping break.
- **Food:** Try **obanzai** for lunch and a simple **kaiseki-style set** or grilled fish dinner.
- **Evening:** **One planned evening activity:** book a **tea ceremony** or a **small-scale cultural performance** in central Kyoto.

### Day 4: Philosopher’s Path Area, Kept Light
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/water.svg
- **Morning:** Start near **Ginkaku-ji** and use a taxi between stops to avoid a long continuous walk.
- **Afternoon:** Visit one additional nearby temple or garden, then finish with café time around **Okazaki** or **Higashiyama**.
- **Food:** Final lunch with **kaisendon**, **udon**, or a Kyoto-style set meal near a transit hub.
- **Evening:** Depart or enjoy a relaxed final dinner close to the hotel.

## Budget Breakdown and Transit-Friendly Costs

| Day | Main Focus | Estimated Cost for 2 | Cost Notes |
|---|---|---:|---|
| Day 1 | Higashiyama temples + Gion | JPY 38,000 | Temple fees, taxi segments, dinner |
| Day 2 | Arashiyama and western Kyoto | JPY 42,000 | Transit, temple entry, lunch, café stop |
| Day 3 | Quiet temples + evening activity | JPY 46,000 | Temple fees, neighborhood meals, tea ceremony/performance |
| Day 4 | Ginkaku-ji area + relaxed finish | JPY 34,000 | Transit, entry fees, lunch, final dinner |
| Buffer | Snacks, extra taxis, contingencies | JPY 20,000 | Helps protect comfort and pace |

**Estimated total: JPY 180,000**

## Comfort-Focused Route Notes

- Use **taxis for short connectors**: station to temple gate, temple to lunch, and end-of-day returns.
- Favor **one major sighting per half-day** instead of stacking multiple long-walk stops.
- Choose hotels near **Kyoto Station, Gion, or Karasuma** for easier transit and fewer transfers.
- Build in **café breaks** after each temple block to reduce knee strain and keep the pace comfortable.

## Packing Checklist for Kyoto in April

- Light jacket or cardigan for cool mornings and evenings
- Comfortable walking shoes with cushioning
- Small umbrella or compact rain shell
- Knee support sleeve if helpful
- Socks that work well with temple footwear rules
- Portable phone charger
- Transit IC card or mobile payment setup
- Reusable water bottle
- Small day bag with room for tickets and tissues
- Basic allergy or pain relief items, if needed

## Useful Planning Links

Action: [Button: Kyoto Transit] https://www.jr-odekake.net/
Action: [Button: Temple Info] https://www.kyoto.travel/en/
Action: [Button: City Buses] https://www.city.kyoto.lg.jp/kotsu/page/0000019452.html

## Sources

- Kyoto official tourism: https://www.kyoto.travel/en/
- Kyoto City transportation: https://www.city.kyoto.lg.jp/kotsu/page/0000019452.html
- JR West travel info: https://www.jr-odekake.net/
